journal.title: Day 1: no citations, no retrieval, and I changed nothing
journal.observed: 0 of 5 target questions cite junhammer.com. For all 5, retrievedInResults is false, sitePagesSeen is empty and position is null. So the site did not appear in the search results at all. Competitors cited: hubspot, dev.to and binatecagency on the ChatGPT question. A crowd of eight (similarweb, profound, airops, frase and others) on SEO vs AEO. Contently, dexcare and healthcare-brew on the health system question. The paragraph-length and citation-mechanics questions had no cited domains at all.
journal.hypothesis: The first problem looks like retrieval, not wording. If the pages are never returned, rewriting them may not help. Possible causes: the pages are not indexed, the pages are too new, or the search tool did not match them to the question. I can't tell which from this data. I also read two pages. The ChatGPT page opens with a long intro and uses topic headings, not question headings. It has no 40 to 60 word direct answer under each heading. The cite-sources page leads with the answer better. That is a real content gap, but I rank it second to retrieval.
journal.action: I read two pages and wrote nothing. The read tool returns only the Markdown body. It hides the front matter. write_file needs the whole file with front matter. I would have to guess the fields, and a wrong guess could break a page in the pull request. I chose not to guess. Next step: rewrite the ChatGPT page. It will have question headings, a direct answer of about 50 words under each, and the answer in the first lines. I'll check whether the front matter can be seen or safely inferred before I do. I spent $0 of the $20.
journal.expect: Nothing should change on this measurement, since I changed nothing. If retrieval stays at 0 of 5 after the first rewrite, I will treat it as an indexing problem that content edits can't fix. I will say so plainly.

journal.title: Day 2: still 0 of 5, and the front matter is still hidden, so I wrote nothing
journal.observed: 0 of 5 questions cite junhammer.com. 0 of 5 retrieved the site at all, and sitePagesSeen is empty for every question. The cited domains are the same as Day 1 (for example mersel.ai, hansvangent.substack.com, straightnorth.com, similarweb.com, contently.com). The lists are longer today, 4 to 8 domains per question instead of 3 to 5. I read that as the measurement showing more of the results, not as the field changing. Day 0 to Day 2 shows no movement for this site.
journal.hypothesis: Zero retrieval on all five questions, including ones where I have a dedicated page, points to an indexing or crawl problem. It does not look like a content-quality problem. If the pages are not in the search index, better headings will not change anything. I can't test this from here. I could be wrong, because a page can be indexed and still never retrieved.
journal.action: I read the ChatGPT page again, /blog/why-your-content-isnt-showing-up-in-chatgpt-answers/. read_page gave me the file path and the Markdown body. It still hides the front matter. write_file replaces the whole file, so I would have to invent the front matter: dates, description, author, and any other fields the template needs. A wrong guess could break the build or reset the publish date. I did not write anything. What I found on the page: it opens with a long paragraph before any answer. Its headings are statements, not questions. It has no 40 to 60 word answer blocks. It has two link placeholders where the text reads "here" and "in this post". That confirms the rewrite I planned. It also tells me what the rewrite must fix. I spent $0 of the $20. $19.81 is left. A request for the human reviewer: if there is a way to show front matter in read_page, or to tell me the fields, that unblocks
journal.expect: No change on Day 3 if I change nothing. After the first rewrite goes live, retrieval for the ChatGPT question should move from 0 to at least 1 within a few days if content is the limit. If it stays at 0 of 5 after the rewrite, I will call it an indexing problem and say so.

journal.title: Day 3: still 0 of 5, and the ChatGPT page already looks fixed, so I changed nothing
journal.observed: 0 of 5 questions cite junhammer.com. 0 of 5 retrieved the site at all, with no site pages seen in any result list. That is the same as Days 0, 1 and 2. Competitors rotate between days (for example scobert.com, itechguides.com and dev.to on the ChatGPT question). The set of cited domains changes, and we are not in it. I re-read /blog/why-your-content-isnt-showing-up-in-chatgpt-answers/. It does not match my Day 2 notes. It now opens with key takeaways and a short answer. It uses question headings, 40 to 60 word answers, real source links and a sources list dated November 18, 2026. I did not write that version, and I can't tell how it got there.
journal.hypothesis: Retrieval is the problem, not citation. The site does not show up in the results at all, so wording is not what is keeping us out. Either the pages are not indexed by the search providers the assistant uses, or the site has too little authority for these competitive queries. The ChatGPT page already has answer-first structure, so a further rewrite would be polish on a page that is not being seen. I'm not certain which cause it is. I can't see indexing status, crawler logs or robots.txt from here.
journal.action: I changed nothing. I read one page and wrote no files. Another edit to the ChatGPT page would not test a new idea, because its structure is already right. The front matter is still hidden from read_page, so a full-file rewrite still means guessing fields. I spent $0. $19.65 is left. Requests for the human reviewer: (1) check that the new pages are indexed in Google and Bing, using Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools; (2) check that robots.txt and the CDN allow OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot; (3) confirm whether the ChatGPT page change was merged, and when. I can't check any of these.
journal.expect: No change on Day 4, since I changed nothing. If retrieval stays at 0 of 5 for several more days on pages that are already well structured, I will treat it as an indexing or authority problem that content edits can't fix. The next content move would then be a new page that targets a narrower question than the big competitive ones, to look for any retrieval at all.

journal.title: Day 4: still 0 of 5, site never retrieved, and I changed nothing again
journal.observed: 0 of 5 cited, 0 of 5 retrieved, no site pages seen for any question. That is the same as Days 0 to 3. The competitors cited change from day to day (for example the ChatGPT question went from mersel.ai and icoda.io on Day 1 to anagram.ai and searchscore.io on Days 3 and 4). The site has not entered the result set for any of the five questions on any day. The 40-word-rule question shows serps.io, lilachbullock.com, kime.ai, airops.com, straightnorth.com and arxiv.org. The health system question has only three cited domains: signalandform.ca, seocheckpilot.com, healthcaresuccess.com.
journal.hypothesis: The most likely cause is that the pages are not in the search index the assistants use, or that the domain has too little authority to be retrieved. Page wording is a weaker explanation. Zero retrieval across five different questions points to a site-level cause. It does not point to five separate content problems. I can't confirm this. I can't see Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, robots.txt or server logs.
journal.action: I changed nothing and spent $0. $19.49 is left. I read the 40-word-rule page. read_page still hides the front matter, and write_file replaces the whole file, so any rewrite would mean guessing fields. What the page shows: (1) most headings are topic labels, such as "Structuring for Information Gain" and "The Bottom Line", and are not questions; (2) the page has no 40 to 60 word answer blocks, which is ironic given its title; (3) it states figures such as "82.5% of ChatGPT citations" and "a factor of 2.7" with no source next to them, and I can't verify them; (4) the closing call to action links to "#", so the link is dead. I will fix these in a rewrite once I can see the front matter. The unsourced statistics should be cited or cut, not kept. Requests for the human reviewer, repeated from Day 3: confirm the pages are indexed in Google and Bing; confirm that OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot
journal.expect: No change on Day 5, since I changed nothing. If I get the front matter, my next move is to rewrite the 40-word-rule page with question headings, 40 to 60 word answers, and sourced or removed statistics. If retrieval is still 0 of 5 a week after a merged rewrite, I will call it an indexing or authority problem that content can't fix.
